t.2.44.1: Having passed through the broad and delightful Kosala lands, the mighty-armed elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa drew near to Śṛṅgaverapura.
t.2.44.2: There Rāghava beheld the Gaṅgā, the divine Tripathagā flowing along three paths, her waters auspicious and free of moss, holy and frequented by ṛṣis.
t.2.44.3: The river resounded with the cries of geese and cranes, echoed with the calls of cakravāka birds, and was frequented by dolphins, crocodiles and serpents.
t.2.44.4: Gazing upon that river, its eddies tumultuous with waves, the great chariot-warrior said to Sumantra the charioteer: "Right here, today, we shall stay."
t.2.44.5: Not far from the river stands this very great iṅgudī tree, rich in flowers and young shoots; here indeed let us dwell, O charioteer.
t.2.44.6: Lakṣmaṇa and Sumantra, having said to Rāghava, "Very well," then went up to that iṅgudī tree with the horses.
t.2.44.7: Having approached that lovely tree, Rāma, the delight of the Ikṣvākus, got down from the chariot together with his wife and with Lakṣmaṇa.
t.2.44.8: Sumantra too, having dismounted and unyoked the excellent horses, approached Rāma, who had gone to the foot of a tree, with joined palms.
t.2.44.9: There ruled a king named Guha, a friend as dear to Rāma as his own self, a mighty man of the Niṣāda clan, renowned as a chieftain.
t.2.44.10: Having heard that Rāma, the tiger among men, had come into his realm, he came to him, surrounded by his aged ministers and his kinsmen.
t.2.44.11: Then Rāma, seeing the lord of the Niṣādas standing at a distance, went together with Saumitri to meet Guha.
t.2.44.12: Distressed, Guha embraced Rāghava and said to him: "As Ayodhyā is yours, so is this land yours, Rāma. What may I do for you?"
t.2.44.13: Then, taking food of excellent quality and of many kinds, he quickly brought it along with the guest-water, and spoke these words.
t.2.44.14: Welcome to you, O mighty-armed one; this entire earth is yours. We are your servants and you are our master; rule well over our kingdom.
t.2.44.15: Here are brought for you foods to be chewed and foods to be eaten, drinks and things to be licked, excellent beds, and fodder for your horses.
t.2.44.16: To Guha, who was speaking thus, Rāghava replied: "We have been honored and gladdened by you in every way."
t.2.44.17: Moved by his coming to meet him on foot and by his show of affection, he pressed him close with his well-shaped arms and spoke these words.
t.2.44.18: By good fortune, Guha, I see you in good health together with your kinsmen. Is all well with you in your kingdom, among your friends, and in your wealth?
t.2.44.19: But whatever you have lovingly prepared here, all of it I give back to you with my leave, for I am not one who accepts gifts.
t.2.44.20: Know me to be an ascetic who wears kuśa grass, bark garments and deerskin, who lives on fruits and roots, who is devoted to dharma and dwells in the forest.
t.2.44.21: I have need only of fodder for the horses and of nothing else; with just this much I shall be well honored by your good self.
t.2.44.22: For these are dear to my father, King Daśaratha; with these horses well cared for, I shall be honored.
t.2.44.23: Right there Guha instructed his men concerning water and fodder for the horses, saying, "Let it be given quickly!"
t.2.44.24: Then, with a garment of bark as his upper cloth, having worshipped the evening twilight, he took as his food only water, brought by Lakṣmaṇa himself.
t.2.44.26: Guha too, together with the charioteer, conversing with Saumitri, then kept watch over Rāma through the night, vigilant and bearing his bow.
t.2.44.25: Lakṣmaṇa washed the feet of him who lay upon the ground with his wife; then, going up to a tree, he stood leaning against it.
t.2.44.27: As the wise, illustrious and great-souled son of Daśaratha lay there thus, he who had never known sorrow and was accustomed to comfort, that night passed for him only slowly.
